title: Wrapper-scoped participant continuity with entry reset
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. Retained wrapper identity and entry-state transfer can be treated as a scope controller: a wrapper at an entry boundary opens a participant/event record, while the same wrapper in an uninterrupted context continues it. Ordered payload components update that record without receiving fixed word meanings.

source_observations: GDT282: opaque outer-wrapper identity transfers across held registers; its claim ceiling excludes lexical or semantic identity.
GDT286: host/context conditioning adds an opaque wrapper variant, with formal gains but no language claim.
GDT318: line-start and preceding-DY selectors jointly compress opaque wrapper entry states across held events.
GDT563: active action/argument state can be carried through repeated context-variable recipes while preserving written atoms.

mechanism.scope_selector: SCOPE(wrapper, line_start, previous_DY, paragraph_boundary) returns NEW_EVENT at a declared entry/reset state and CONTINUE otherwise. The selector is fixed before reading content.
mechanism.open: NEW_EVENT(wrapper,payload) creates ACTIVE_RECORD(wrapper, participant_opaque, payload, open_state).
mechanism.carry: CONTINUE(wrapper,payload,active_record) preserves participant_opaque and appends/updates the payload in written order; it cannot select a nearest noun or invent a missing participant.
mechanism.reset: At an explicit paragraph/entry reset, CLOSE(active_record) ends the prior record before NEW_EVENT can create another one.
mechanism.payload_rule: Known component order and exact whole-form residual remain formal payload structure. They do not decide participant identity by themselves.

design.complete_reading_consequence: A complete passage with two clauses in one uninterrupted wrapper context must share one opaque participant/event record across the clauses; a line-start or declared paragraph reset must create a new record even when the payload form repeats. A three-clause passage can therefore OPEN one record, CONTINUE it with a second ordered payload, and CLOSE it at the next written reset.
design.falsifier: On a predeclared set of complete passages, reject the model if repeated wrappers in the same selector context require distinct participants, if entry/reset contexts do not predict record breaks beyond matched context frequencies, or if a continuation needs an unprinted nearest-reference repair.
design.strongest_failure: GDT282/286/318 establish transferable opaque form/context channels, not participant identity. IVTFF line and paragraph boundaries can be editorial, and GDT563's inherited action/argument state is a working renderer. Without an independently owned participant relation, continuity may be a formal compression artifact.

predecessors.limit: Wrapper identity transfers formally; no semantic class is imported.
Host-context variant has a failed position increment gate; only opaque context conditioning is retained.
Entry-state compression supplies the selector family but no participant meaning.
Active state carry is a working edition; this proposal adds an explicit record identity/reset consequence.
Carrier-chain card assigns local opener/pivot/closer roles; this proposal uses wrapper scope and record continuity instead.

dependencies: Wrapper class and entry/reset context must be fixed from retained formal observations.
A complete passage must contain at least two same-context occurrences and one explicit reset comparison.
Participant identity remains opaque; no target word, image role, or historical source name is assigned.
No source or target nearest-reference rule may be added after seeing an outcome.
design.access: Retained reports and route/duplicate checks only; no new target rows, images, reserves, GDT1001/source packet, decoder, experiment, route, ledger, or publication.
